- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model underestimates upside — add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–4% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction — subtract 1–2% from next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3 consecutive days below 70), model tends to overpredict — reduce forecast by 1–3%.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from negative to positive (e.g., 0.2 → 0.8), model lags — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
